The process begins when the customer is hungry.

First, the customer chooses a pizza from the menu. After making their selection, the customer orders the pizza by phone.

Once the order is placed, the customer faces a decision: either wait or inquire about the order. If the customer decides to wait, they wait for 60 minutes. After waiting, the customer checks whether the pizza has arrived. If the pizza has arrived, the process continues; if the pizza has not arrived, the customer calls the pizzeria to inquire about the status.

Alternatively, if the customer initially chooses to inquire rather than wait, they call the pizzeria to inquire about the status directly. After inquiring, the customer then checks again whether the pizza has arrived.

Once the pizza arrives, the customer pays the delivery boy. Following payment, the customer eats the pizza, and the process concludes with the customer's hunger being satisfied.

The process begins when a customer order is initiated at GBI's Sales Department.

First, the Sales Department creates customer master data, then updates the customer data. Meanwhile, at The Bike Zone, the customer initiates a request and sends it to the Sales Department. Upon receiving this communication, the Sales Department accepts and processes the request, then processes an offer and copies the offer to an order, sending it to the customer.

The customer at The Bike Zone receives and accepts the offer, processes it, then orders bicycles and sends the order back to the Sales Department. The Sales Department accepts and processes this order, which triggers the Material Management department to check inventory.

Based on the inventory check, if the product is in stock, Material Management requests the product. If the product is not in stock, they procure and order the goods. Either path then converges, and the Sales Department processes the customer order and creates a delivery note.

Material Management then performs inventory control, after which the Sales Department picks the material, packs it, and sends the goods to the customer. The customer at The Bike Zone registers the goods receipt.

After sending the goods, two activities happen simultaneously: Material Management checks inventory while the Finance Department creates an invoice and sends it to the customer. The customer receives the invoice and settles it, sending payment information back to GBI. Once both the inventory check and the invoice sending are complete, the Finance Department processes the incoming payment.

Finally, the Sales Department edits and displays the document flow, and the process is completed.

1.text:
The process describes a customer order workflow between The Bike Zone (a customer) and GBI (a supplier company with Sales, Material Management, and Finance departments).

The process begins at GBI's Sales Department when a customer order is initiated. First, customer master data is created, followed by updating the customer data. Meanwhile, the customer at The Bike Zone initiates a request and sends it to the Sales Department. Upon receiving this request, the Sales Department accepts and processes it, then processes an offer and copies the offer to an order. The offer is then sent to the customer.

The customer receives and processes the offer, then decides to order bicycles and sends the order to the Sales Department. The Sales Department accepts and processes the order, which triggers the Material Management department to check inventory. Based on this check, if the product is in stock, the product is requested internally; if the product is not in stock, goods must be procured or ordered externally. After either path is completed, the process continues with processing the customer order.

The Sales Department then creates a delivery note, after which Material Management performs inventory control. The Sales Department picks the material and packs it, then sends the goods to the customer. The customer registers the goods receipt upon delivery.

After sending the goods, two activities happen simultaneously: Material Management checks inventory after sending goods, while the Finance Department creates an invoice and sends it to the customer. The customer receives the invoice and settles it, sending payment back to GBI. Once both the inventory check and the invoice sending are complete, the Finance Department processes the incoming payment. Finally, the Sales Department edits and displays the document flow, and the process is completed.

The process begins when an email account is needed within the Email Account Creation Portal.

First, the user logs on to the email provider's website. After logging on, the user chooses a package for their email account. The system then automatically checks if a personal account is available.

At this point, a decision is made based on the availability of the personal account. If the personal account is not available, the process ends with the private account being unavailable.

If the personal account is available, the user enters the private account welcome page and provides personal information. Following this, two activities occur simultaneously: the user enters their full names, and the user uploads a photo ID. Both of these tasks must be completed before proceeding.

Once both the full names have been entered and the photo ID has been uploaded, the user confirms their personal data. After confirmation, the system automatically generates a new email ID and password. The process then concludes successfully with the private email being created.

The process at SoKnow begins when corporate designs are identified as outdated by the Marketing Department.

The Marketing Department then conducts a brainstorming session to generate ideas for the new designs. Following this, the Designers take over and design a new element based on the brainstorming outcomes. Once the design is complete, the Designers review the design.

After the review, a decision is made regarding whether the design is satisfactory. If the design is not satisfactory, the Designers revise the design and then create a new design again. If the design is satisfactory, the Designers proceed to create templates based on the approved design.

The templates are then reviewed by the Marketing Department. Following this review, a decision is made on whether the templates are satisfactory. If the templates are not satisfactory, the Designers revise the design and the process loops back to designing a new element. If the templates are satisfactory, the Marketing Department conducts communication with management to seek approval.

After presenting to management, a decision is made on whether management approves the new corporate designs. If management does not approve, the Designers revise the design and the process returns to the design phase. If management approves, the Marketing Department begins to use the new corporate designs.

The process concludes when the new corporate designs are officially in use.

The process begins when an undergraduate student starts their application for the IMIS (International Management Information Systems) program.

First, the student goes to the FH-SWF website and proceeds to define their search criteria. At this point, three selections must be made simultaneously: selecting Master Study Course as the degree type, selecting Informatics and Digitalisation as the subject area, and selecting Campus Soest as the location. Once all three criteria have been selected, the student clicks on "Find a Study Course."

After the search results appear, the student clicks on "Learn more" on the IMIS banner, then selects the Master Study Course, and clicks on "See how to apply here" to view the application instructions.

The application path then diverges depending on the applicant's status. For non-EU or international applicants, the student must apply via Uni-Assist, check the application procedure, send the required documents to Uni-Assist, and then wait for a decision within 10-12 weeks before receiving an admission or rejection letter.

For EU applicants, there is a further distinction based on whether they are current or former FH-SWF students. If the applicant is not an FH-SWF student or graduate, they must apply via the FH-SWF Online Portal, send the required documents, and contact the IMIS office. If the applicant is an FH-SWF student or graduate, they apply via the FH-SWF Online Portal and contact the IMIS office directly. In both EU applicant scenarios, after completing these steps, the student waits for a decision within 4-6 weeks.

Regardless of which application path was followed, the process concludes with the receipt of an admission or rejection letter.

Jane Doe first checks the feasibility of the order. If the order is determined to be not feasible, the process is aborted through escalation and ends there.

If the offer is not accepted, Jane Doe informs the customer that no order confirmation will be issued, and the process ends with the customer being informed accordingly.

If the offer is accepted, Jane Doe creates the order and enters it into production planning. Following this, the order confirmation is sent, and the process concludes with the order confirmation being dispatched.

The process begins at DLL when a loan application is initiated.

The Risk Manager starts by performing two checks simultaneously: a BKR check and a Jane Doe check. Both checks must be completed before the process can continue.

Once both checks are finished, the results are evaluated to determine if both assessments are accepted. If the assessments are not accepted, the Administrator sends a rejection letter to the client, and the process ends with a rejection.

If both assessments are accepted, the Senior Risk Manager performs a credibility check. After completing this check, the credibility is evaluated. If the credibility is not confirmed, a rejection letter is sent to the client by the Administrator, ending the process. If the credibility is confirmed, the Senior Risk Manager reviews the credibility assessment.

Following the review, the assessment outcome is evaluated. If the assessment is not accepted, the Administrator sends a rejection letter to the client, concluding the process. If the assessment is accepted, the Customer Relation Team calls the client to complement information.

If the client does not pick up the call, the team waits one hour and then attempts to call the client again. This cycle continues until the client answers. Once the client picks up, a loan offer is created, then checked, and subsequently sent to the client.

The process then waits for the client to accept the offer. If the offer is not accepted within one hour, the client is reminded, and the process loops back to wait for the client's response again. Once the offer is accepted, the Administrator sends a welcome letter to the client.

The Finance Department then activates the loan application, validates the loan activation, and executes the initial payment. Finally, the Administrator returns the documents to the client, and the process ends successfully as completed.

The process begins when lunch break begins for Frank at Global Car Manufacturing Inc.

Frank first chooses his preferred lunch, then decides between pizza or noodles.

If Frank chooses pizza, he selects an order method. He can either order online by accessing the website, or order by phone by calling the pizza delivery person. Regardless of the method chosen, Frank then places the order, which is communicated to the Pizza Delivery Person. After placing the order, Frank waits for the pizza.

Meanwhile, at Pizza Delivery, the Pizza Delivery Person receives the order, prepares the pizza, and then delivers it. Upon arrival, the Pizza Delivery Person hands over the pizza to Frank.

While Frank is waiting, he receives the pizza from the delivery person. Frank then pays for the pizza, and the Pizza Delivery Person accepts the payment. After this exchange, Frank's lunch break ends.

If Frank chooses noodles instead, he starts the preparation. Two activities then happen simultaneously: Frank boils water and prepares the sauce. After boiling the water, Frank adds the noodles and cooks them for eight minutes. Concurrently, the sauce cooks for ten minutes. Once both the noodles and sauce are ready, Frank mixes them together and then eats his meal. After finishing, the lunch break ends.

Regardless of the method chosen, Frank then places his order, which is communicated to the Pizza Delivery service.

Upon receiving the order, the pizza delivery person prepares the pizza, then delivers it, and hands it over to Frank. Frank receives the pizza and pays for it, with the payment being accepted by the pizza delivery person. After this, Frank's lunch break ends.

If Frank chooses noodles instead, he starts the preparation process. At this point, two activities happen simultaneously: he boils water and prepares the sauce. Once the water is boiling, he adds the noodles and cooks them for eight minutes. Concurrently, the sauce cooks for ten minutes. After both the noodles and sauce are ready, Frank mixes them together and then eats his meal. Following this, his lunch break ends.

The process begins within Outdoor Operations when a task arises, handled initially by Technical Jane Doe.

First, the working time effort is estimated, followed by checking the availability of resources. Once resources are confirmed, a field employee is selected and contacted. Technical Jane Doe then checks if the employee is reachable.

If the employee is not reachable, the task is marked as not assigned, and the process loops back to check the availability of resources again, repeating the cycle of selecting and contacting a field employee until one is successfully reached.

If the employee is reachable, the task is assigned to that employee, and the procedure for task completion is specified.

At this point, the work transitions to the Field Employee, who receives the task and confirms it. The field employee then processes the task, completes it, and makes a completion report.

The completion report is then sent back to Technical Jane Doe, who documents the completion report. The process concludes with the task being marked as processed.

The loan application process begins and immediately splits into two parallel activities performed by Risk Management: a BKR check and a Jane Doe check are conducted simultaneously.

Once both checks are completed, the results are merged and Risk Management confirms the credibility check. This confirmation is then reviewed by Senior Risk Management, who also confirms the credibility check.

Based on the assessment decision, the process takes one of two paths. If the application is rejected, Administration sends a rejection letter to the client, and the process ends with the rejection.

If the application is accepted, Customer Contact attempts to call the client to complement information. If the call is not picked up, the process waits for one hour to pass before attempting to call the client again. This retry loop continues until the call is successfully picked up.

Once the client answers the call, Customer Contact creates and sends a loan offer to the client. The process then enters a waiting phase where it monitors for the client's response. If two hours pass without receiving an accepted offer, Finance reminds the client, and the process returns to waiting for the offer. This reminder loop continues until the accepted offer is received.

When the accepted offer is received, Administration sends a welcome letter to the client. Following this, Finance activates the loan application, validates the activation, and executes the initial payment. Finally, Administration returns the documents to the client, and the process completes successfully.

The process begins at SoKnow when personnel accounting needs to be managed, handled entirely by the Personnel Administration department.

First, the payroll program is started. Following this, automated debits are controlled to ensure accuracy. Once the debits have been verified, labor costs are calculated.

After calculating labor costs, two activities are performed simultaneously: salaries and social contributions are paid, while at the same time health insurance and additional costs are paid. Both payment activities must be completed before the process continues.

Once both payment streams are finished, bonuses are entered into the system. Subsequently, financial accounting is controlled to verify all entries and transactions. Finally, an invoice is sent, and the process concludes with personnel accounting being completed.

First, management sends invitations to the employees. Once the invitations are sent, two activities occur simultaneously: management leads the annual planning meeting while employees participate in the meeting.

After both the leading and participation in the meeting are completed, management conducts a review and discussion of the current strategy. Following this review, two parallel activities commence: management reformulates the strategy while employees align for the strategy.

Once both the strategy reformulation and alignment are finished, management communicates the reformulated strategy. Subsequently, management pursues the reformulated strategy, and the process concludes with the annual meeting upcoming.

The process at SoKnown begins when a late payment is received, which triggers the Finance Department to inform management.

After management is informed, a check is made to determine whether a reminder has already been sent to the customer. 

If a reminder has already been sent, the Finance Department makes an inquiry with the customer and then sends an inquiry email. This email is communicated to the Customer Company. Following this, the process waits to see if a response is received. If a response is received, the Finance Department performs an online banking check, posts the payment, and the process ends with the payment being processed.

If no response is received after the inquiry email, the Finance Department notifies a lawyer, and a request for legal assistance is sent to the External Lawyer. The reminder process is then run, and the process concludes with the payment being processed.

If no reminder has been sent yet, the Legal Department creates a reminder and sends it to the Customer Company. After the reminder is sent, a check is made to determine whether payment has been made. If payment has been made, the Legal Department completes the reminder process, and then the Finance Department posts the payment, ending the process with the payment being processed.

If payment has not been made, the Legal Department creates another reminder. At this point, a check is made to see if this is the third unsuccessful reminder. If the third reminder has been unsuccessful, the Finance Department is notified, which then notifies a lawyer and sends a request for legal assistance to the External Lawyer, followed by running the reminder process and concluding with the payment being processed. If the reminders should continue, the process loops back to check again whether payment has been made, allowing for additional reminders to be sent.

The process begins at SoKnown when a late payment is received by the Finance Department.

First, management is informed about the late payment situation. Then, a check is made to determine whether a reminder has already been sent to the customer.

If a reminder has already been sent, the Finance Department makes an inquiry with the customer, and an inquiry email is automatically sent to the Customer Company. Based on whether a response is received, the process takes different paths. If a response is received, an online banking check is performed, followed by posting the payment, and the process ends with the payment being processed.

If no response is received from the customer, the Finance Department notifies a lawyer, and a request for legal assistance is automatically sent to the External Lawyer. The Legal Department then runs the reminder process, and the process concludes with the payment being processed.

The process begins when a patient receives a prescription.

First, a check is made to determine whether the prescription is for the patient themselves. If the prescription is not for the patient themselves, the prescription remains unfilled and the process ends.

If the prescription is for the patient themselves, the patient shows their Medicare card and prescriptions to the pharmacist at NewTown Health Chemist. The pharmacist receives and checks the script details. If the prescription is not valid, the prescription remains unfilled and the process ends.

If the prescription is valid, the pharmacist opens and reviews the patient profile in the pharmacy information system, then views the prescription information and checks if the patient is suspicious.

If the patient is deemed suspicious, the pharmacist contacts the GP for advice. The doctor replies via email or call with advice and recommendations, which the pharmacist receives. The pharmacist then confirms the decision, and the prescription remains unfilled, ending the process.

If the patient is not suspicious, the pharmacist checks the patient's status including allergies, pregnancy, and past history. If the status check is not passed, the pharmacist offers alternatives with a lower dosage level. If the patient agrees to the alternatives, the pharmacist adds a short memo and proceeds. If the patient does not agree to the alternatives, the prescription remains unfilled and the process ends.

If the status check is passed, the pharmacist selects the correct prescribed dosage and checks the prescription inventory. If the medication is out of stock, the pharmacist informs the patient about alternatives and then proceeds. If the medication is in stock, the pharmacist double-checks and collects the correct drugs.

Following any of these paths that continue, Medicare costs, waivers, and total fees are calculated automatically, and the pharmacist prints and attaches labels with consumer medicine information. This information is communicated to the patient, who receives consultation and recommendations on timing, pays the prescription fees, receives the prescriptions, and the dispensing process ends.

The process begins at SoKnow when a new marketing campaign is initiated in the Marketing Department.

First, Management plans the focal points for the campaign. Once the focal points are established, the Marketing Department designs ideas and defines specifications. After completing the specifications, the Marketing Department sends the order to the external marketing agency.

Upon receiving the order, the External Marketing Agency is commissioned and begins creating drafts. Once the drafts are completed, the agency sends them back to the marketing department.

The Marketing Department receives and evaluates the drafts, then puts them to a vote. Based on the vote result, the process takes one of two paths.

If the vote is negative, the Marketing Department asks the agency for new drafts. This request is communicated to the External Marketing Agency, which creates new drafts and sends them back. The Marketing Department then receives and evaluates these new drafts again, repeating the voting cycle.

If the vote is positive, the Marketing Department informs Management. Management then re-evaluates the drafts and makes a decision.

If Management's evaluation is negative, they ask the agency for new drafts. This request is sent to the External Marketing Agency, which creates new drafts and sends them back to the Marketing Department for another round of evaluation and voting.

If Management's evaluation is positive, they give the Marketing Department the green light. This approval is also communicated to the External Marketing Agency, which is commissioned for execution. The Marketing Department then conducts the campaign, and the process concludes with the marketing campaign being completed.

If the applicant is suitable, two activities occur simultaneously: scheduling an appointment with the applicant for the assessment center and planning and preparing the assessment center. Once both activities are completed, the assessment center is conducted, after which the process proceeds to taking a vote on the applicant.

After the vote is taken, a final decision is made. The process takes place within the Accounting and Controlling department and begins at a start point.

First, the booking system is created, followed by starting the booking system. Once the system is running, the payment is read, and then payment automation is initiated.

At this point, a check is made to determine whether the payment has been made. If the payment has been made, the payment is booked, and the process concludes with the payment having been made.

If the payment has not been made, a reminder is sent. After sending the reminder, another check occurs to determine whether the payment has been made following the reminder. If the payment has been made after the reminder, the payment is booked, and the process ends with the payment having been made.

However, if the payment has still not been made after the reminder, a written dunning procedure is initiated. The reminder notice is then reviewed. If the review is successful, the reminder notice is sent, and the process concludes with the reminder notice having been sent.

If the review is not successful, the reminder notice must be correctly filled out, after which it is reviewed again. This cycle of correcting and reviewing continues until the review is successful, at which point the reminder notice is sent and the process ends.

The process begins at ACME AG's Procurement Department when a need arises for work equipment.

First, the stock is checked to determine availability. If the work equipment is in stock, it is retrieved from the storeroom, and the process concludes with the work equipment being removed from the storeroom.

If the work equipment is not in stock, the requirements are specified and quantified. Following this, an order is placed.

After placing the order, the process waits to determine whether a receipt is received within five days. If a receipt is received before the five-day period elapses, the process concludes with the work equipment being procured.

However, if five days pass without receiving a receipt, the process waits for this duration to complete, and then an order is placed by e-mail directly to the supplier. Once this automated order is sent, the work equipment is received manually, and the process ends with the work equipment being successfully procured.

The process begins when a customer starts their purchasing journey by selecting and buying goods online.

Once the customer completes their online purchase, this information is communicated to the company's Finance Department, where they check if a creditworthiness check is required.

If a credit check is required, the Finance Department requests the necessary information and then assesses the customer's creditworthiness. If the customer is found to be creditworthy, the process continues forward. However, if the customer is not creditworthy, the Finance Department informs the customer about the rejection, and the process ends with the order being declined.

If no credit check is required, or if the customer passes the creditworthiness assessment, the Finance Department informs the warehouse about the shipping request.

The Warehouse then checks if the item is available in stock. If the item is not available, a reorder is triggered, and the availability check is performed again once stock is replenished. This cycle continues until the item becomes available.

Once the item is available, the Warehouse packs the item and then ships it. Upon shipping, the customer receives both the purchase and shipping confirmation, which concludes the process successfully.

Throughout this process, there are three key communications between the customer and the company: the initial purchase order from the customer triggers the company's internal processing, any rejection notification is sent from the Finance Department to the customer, and finally, the shipping confirmation is sent from the Warehouse to the customer upon successful delivery of the item.

The process begins in the Service Department of the Organization when a customer application is recorded. Following this, the order is recorded by the same department.

The order then moves to the Finance Department, where the customer data is checked. At this point, a decision is made based on whether the data is correct.

If the data is correct, the order is released by the Finance Department, and then the order is communicated to the Service Department.

If the data is incorrect, the order is rejected by the Finance Department. The Service Department then informs the customer, and the process ends with the customer being informed.

When the Service Department receives the communicated order, they receive the order, then process it, print it, and finally forward it. The process concludes with the order being forwarded.

If the data is correct, the Finance Department releases the order and then communicates the order to the Service Department.

If the data is not correct, the Finance Department rejects the order. The rejection is then communicated back to the Service Department, which informs the customer about the outcome. The process ends with the customer being informed.

When the Service Department receives the communicated order from the Finance Department, they proceed to process the order. After processing, the order is printed and then forwarded. The process concludes with the order being forwarded.

The process begins within the Purchasing Team when the need for software licenses arises.

First, the team defines the requirements for the licenses needed. Once the requirements are established, they proceed to select the appropriate licenses. After selecting the licenses, they check whether the system has been executed previously.

Based on this check, the process takes one of two paths: if the system has been executed, the team proceeds to purchase the license directly; if the system has not been executed, they buy a test license instead. Regardless of which path was taken, both converge and the team then agrees upon framework contracts.

Following the framework contract agreement, a license purchase agreement is created. At this point, two activities happen simultaneously: the license purchase contract data is provided automatically by the system, and the contract information is updated manually. Once both of these parallel activities are completed, the team places the order.

After the order is placed, the final acceptance of delivery occurs. The team then reviews the framework agreements and subsequently updates the system. Following the system update, the Purchasing Team forwards the payment, which concludes their part of the process with the license being purchased.

The payment forwarding triggers a communication to the Accounting/Controlling department, who then executes the payment. This final step concludes the overall process with the payment being executed.

The process begins when a customer decides to dine at a restaurant.

The customer places an order for food, which is communicated to the waiter. The waiter receives the order from the customer and then sends the order to the sous chef in the kitchen.

The sous chef receives the order from the waiter and proceeds to manage the order of cooking, determining the sequence and timing of preparation. Once organized, the sous chef passes the cooking task to the chef.

The chef receives the cooking task and prepares the food accordingly. After cooking is complete, the chef sends the food to the sous chef for checking.

The sous chef receives the food from the chef and checks it to ensure quality and correctness. Once satisfied, the sous chef calls the waiter to grab the food.

The waiter responds by grabbing the food from the kitchen and then delivers the food to the customer at their table.

The customer receives the food and proceeds to enjoy the meal. Once the customer has finished enjoying the food, the process ends.

The customer places an order for food, which is then communicated to the waiter at the restaurant. The waiter receives the order from the customer and subsequently sends the order to the kitchen.

In the kitchen, the sous chef receives the order from the waiter and manages the order of cooking. The sous chef then passes the task to the chef, communicating what needs to be prepared.

The chef cooks the food and, once completed, sends the food for checking back to the sous chef. The sous chef checks the food to ensure quality and, when satisfied, calls the waiter to grab the food.

The waiter receives this notification and grabs the food from the kitchen. The waiter then delivers the food to the customer.

The customer receives the food from the waiter and proceeds to enjoy the meal. Once the customer has finished enjoying the food, the process ends.

The process at Startup TUd-03 begins in the Warehousing Department when a need for goods arises.

First, a bill of materials is created, followed by ordering the goods. After placing the order, a check is made to determine whether an inquiry has been received from the supplier. If an inquiry is received, the question is clarified with the specialist department before awaiting delivery. If no inquiry is received, the process proceeds directly to awaiting delivery.

While awaiting delivery, the process checks whether the delivery arrives within five working days. If the delivery arrives in time, the parts are received from the supplier and the process continues with checking the quantity and quality of the goods. If the delivery does not arrive within five days, the supplier is contacted to check if immediate shipping is possible. If immediate shipping is possible, the process returns to awaiting delivery. If immediate shipping is not possible, the process ends with an escalation of delivery issues.

Once the parts are delivered and inspected, a determination is made whether the quantity and quality meet standards. If the standards are not met, a replacement delivery is requested, and this replacement request is communicated to the supplier. The process then returns to awaiting delivery for the replacement. If the standards are met, the goods are stored.

After storing the goods, the process moves to the Sales Department, where the order is transmitted. The goods are then prepared and packaged, followed by shipping or issuing the goods. The process concludes successfully at this point.

Throughout this process, the Supplier communicates with the Warehousing Department by sending inquiries and delivering parts, and receives replacement requests when quality or quantity issues arise.

The process begins at Hochschule Mainz Support when a request for support is received by the Support Team.

First, the team receives the ticket and then determines whether customer participation is necessary to resolve the issue.

If customer participation is not necessary, the team proceeds to solve the problem independently without involving the customer. After resolving the issue, notes are created for documentation purposes, and a confirmation is sent to indicate that the ticket is completed. The process then ends with the problem being solved.

If customer participation is required, the team contacts the customer and conducts a detailed interview about the problem. Following this, the team connects to the customer's client system and attempts to solve the problem together with the customer.

At this point, a decision is made regarding whether further information is needed. If additional information is required, the team asks for further information and then returns to trying to solve the problem together with the customer. This cycle continues until no further information is needed.

Once no further information is required, the team proceeds to solve the problem. After the solution is implemented, notes are created for documentation, and a confirmation is sent to the customer indicating that the ticket has been completed. The process then concludes with the problem being solved.

The process begins at ACME AG when an application is received by the HR Department.

Upon receiving the application, the HR Department sends an acknowledgment of receipt to the applicant. Following this, the HR Department checks the applicant's credentials and qualifications. The information is then passed to the HR Manager, who determines the application status.

Based on the application status, the process takes one of two paths. If the application is rejected, the HR Department sends a rejection notice to the applicant, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

If the application is accepted, the HR Department sends an invitation to a job interview to the applicant. Concurrently, the HR Department prepares an employment contract. The HR Department then conducts the job interview with the applicant.

After the interview, the HR Manager determines the applicant's suitability for the position. If the applicant is deemed not suitable, the HR Department sends a rejection notice, and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

If the applicant is found suitable, the HR Department sends the prepared employment contract to the applicant. The process concludes when the HR Department receives the signed employment contract back from the applicant, marking the successful completion of the hiring process with a signed employment contract available.

The process begins when a doctor plans a discharge within the department.

First, the doctor sets the discharge date. Following this, three activities are initiated simultaneously: the doctor discusses the further course of action with the patient and relatives, the doctor determines the medical care needs, and the nursing staff assesses the nursing care needs.

Once all three of these parallel activities are completed, the doctor defines the supply facility. After this, two activities begin in parallel: the doctor creates a doctor's letter, and the doctor checks whether social services are required.

If social services are required, the nursing staff initiates further care services, and then the nursing staff creates the discharge documentation. If social services are not required, the process proceeds directly without these additional nursing tasks.

Once the doctor's letter has been created and the social services path has been resolved (either after creating the discharge documentation or after determining that social services are not needed), the doctor carries out advanced tasks for discharge.

The process concludes when the discharge is completed.

The process begins within the Request Fulfillment Process when a request is initiated.

First, the Incident Manager verifies the request. After verification, an order is sent for request handling. The 1st Level Support then receives the order and proceeds to log and categorize the request.

At this point, a decision is made regarding whether the request is authorized. If the request is not authorized, it is sent back to the Incident Manager to verify the request again. If the request is authorized, the process splits into two parallel activities.

Simultaneously, the Incident Manager handles request monitoring and escalation while the 1st Level Support (along with the Service Request Fulfillment Group) executes the model execution requested. Both of these activities must be completed before the process can continue.

Once both parallel tasks are finished, they merge and the request closure and evaluation takes place. Following this evaluation, a check is made to determine if there is a problem with the request.

If there is no problem, request fulfillment support is provided, and the process concludes successfully.

If a problem is identified, the Incident Manager contacts the incident manager about the problem, and the process ends with the indication that it ended with a problem.

The process begins in the HR Department when an HR Clerk starts the co-signature note workflow.

First, the HR Clerk retrieves the requirement profile, followed by retrieving the job posting. Once both documents are gathered, the clerk creates and forwards a co-signature note to the Section Manager.

The Section Manager then reviews the note. If the Section Manager has comments, the note is returned to the clerk, who then creates and forwards a new co-signature note back to the Section Manager for another review. This cycle continues until the Section Manager has no further comments.

When the Section Manager has no comments, the note is forwarded to the Department Head. The Department Head then reviews the note. If the Department Head has comments, the note is sent back to the Section Manager, who creates and forwards a new co-signature note to the Department Head for another review. This cycle between the Section Manager and Department Head continues until the Department Head has no further comments.

Once the Department Head has no comments, the process ends, indicating that the co-signature note has been fully approved through all levels of review within the HR Department.

The process begins at the Savings Bank when an application arrives at the HR Team.

Upon receiving the application, the HR Team sends a receipt confirmation to the applicant and then reviews the application. After the review, a decision is made regarding whether the application is in order.

If the application is not in order, the HR Team rejects the applicant and sends a rejection notice to the applicant, concluding the process with the applicant being rejected.

If the application is in order, it is forwarded to the IT Department for evaluation. The IT Department evaluates the application and determines whether the applicant is suitable for the position.

If the applicant is not suitable, the IT Department rejects the applicant and sends a rejection notice, ending the process with the applicant being rejected.

If the applicant is suitable, the process returns to the HR Team, who invites the applicant for an interview. The HR Team then prepares for the interview and conducts it. Should the applicant decline the invitation at this stage, the application documents are archived and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

Following the interview, a decision is made about whether the applicant performed well. If the applicant is not considered good, they are rejected, a rejection notice is sent, and the application documents are archived, ending the process with the applicant being rejected.

If the applicant is deemed good, they are placed on a list, and then selected. The HR Team then obtains approval from the board of directors. If approval is not granted, the applicant is rejected, a rejection notice is sent, the application documents are archived, and the process concludes with the applicant being rejected.

If approval is granted, the HR Team confirms the applicant, prepares the contract, and the contract is signed. The applicant is then placed in the position, and the position is occupied in the system, concluding the process with the applicant being hired.

At any point after confirmation, if the applicant declines the position, the application documents are archived and the process ends with the applicant being rejected.

The process begins when a client initiates a new service by entering the store and looking for a specific service.

If the service is not found, the process ends immediately with the service not being available.

If the service is found, the client takes a ticket representing their turn. At this point, the process diverges based on where the ticket was taken.

If the ticket was taken in the app, the client waits for the waiting time, then looks for the product and specific criteria, and subsequently checks how many tickets are ahead until their turn. After this, the paths merge.

If the ticket was taken physically, the client simply waits for their turn, after which the paths merge.

Once the paths converge, the client asks for a specific request. This request is communicated to the Request Assistant at the Service Provider.

When the register time expires, the Request Assistant registers the request and then checks if there are enough requests to respond to customer demand.

If there are not enough requests, the assistant continues to register additional requests in a loop.

If there are enough requests, the order request document is sent to the Shop Assistants Team, and the registering phase ends.

Upon receiving the order request document, the Shop Assistants Team prepares the order. Once preparation is complete, the order is delivered to the client, concluding the preparation phase.

The client receives notification when the order is prepared and delivered, then collects the order, and the process ends with the order successfully collected.

The process begins when the program starts within the AO-Software system.

First, the program starts for the player, and then the user is asked if they want to start the tutorial. If the user chooses yes, a tutorial on controller functions is started. If the user declines, the system begins with the standard key assignment.

After either path, the user is presented with a menu selection offering four options: continue a game, load a saved game, start a new game, or access game settings.

If the user chooses to continue a game, the game resumes from where it was last ended. If the user chooses to load a saved game, the saved game data is retrieved, and the game continues from the saved point. Both of these paths then proceed forward.

If the user chooses to start a new game, they are guided through a tutorial on controller functions, and then asked if they want to start the game with standard key assignment. If they agree, the process continues forward. If they decline, they are returned to the menu selection to make another choice.

If the user chooses to access game settings, they are returned to the menu selection after making their adjustments.

Once the user has made their selection and completed the necessary steps, two activities occur simultaneously: ambient noise is generated and background music begins playing. After both audio elements are active, the game is loaded, the user is prompted for input, and the user provides their input.

The process concludes when the game begins.

First, the program starts for the player, and then the user is asked if they want to start the tutorial. If the user chooses yes, a tutorial on controller functions is started. If the user declines, the system begins with the standard key assignment. After either path, the user is presented with a menu selection.

From the menu, the user can choose one of four options: continue a game, load a saved game, start a new game, or access game settings.

If the user chooses to continue a game, the game resumes from where it was last ended, and then the process proceeds toward starting the game.

If the user chooses to load a saved game, the saved game data is retrieved, and then the game continues from the saved point before proceeding toward starting the game.

If the user chooses to start a new game, they are guided through a tutorial on controller functions. Afterward, the user is asked if they want to start the game with the standard key assignment. If they agree, the process moves forward to start the game. If they decline, they are returned to the menu selection to make another choice.

If the user chooses to access game settings, they can adjust settings and are then returned to the menu selection.

Once the user is ready to start the game, the system simultaneously generates ambient noise and plays background music. After both audio elements are active, the game is loaded, and the user is prompted for input. The player then provides input, and the process concludes with the game beginning.

If the player chooses to start a new game, they are asked if they want to start the game with the standard key assignment. If they decline, they are returned to the menu selection to make another choice. If they accept, the process continues toward starting the game.

If the player chooses to access game settings, they can adjust settings and are then returned to the menu selection.

Once a game mode has been selected and confirmed (whether continuing, loading, or starting new with standard keys), the system simultaneously generates ambient noise and plays background music. After both audio elements are active, the game is loaded. The system then prompts the user for input, the user provides their input, and the game begins.

The SoKnow process begins when the HR Department initiates the process.

First, the HR Department organizes employee interviews, and then sends appointment suggestions to the employees.

After sending the appointment suggestions, two parallel paths of activities commence. On the HR Department side, the employee interview is conducted while simultaneously regular inquiries are made. Following the interview, training is assigned to the employee. Both the interview-related activities and the regular inquiries must complete before the HR Department's portion concludes with the employee interview being marked as conducted.

On the Employee side, upon receiving the appointment suggestions, three activities happen in parallel: the employee confirms the appointment, participates in the interview, and completes the assigned training. All three activities must be finished before the Employee's portion of the process ends with the training being marked as completed.

Throughout this process, there is communication between the HR Department and the Employee. The appointment suggestions sent by HR are received by the employee who then confirms the appointment. When the HR Department conducts the employee interview, the employee participates in that same interview. Additionally, when HR assigns training, the employee receives this assignment and completes the training accordingly.

The process begins when a user comes to the library.

First, the user is logged in, and then their request is determined.

Depending on the type of request, the process follows different paths. If the user wants to extend media, the process for extending media is initiated. If the extension is successful, the process ends with the media being extended. If the extension is not successful, the process ends with the medium being returned.

Alternatively, if the user wants to borrow a medium, they select the desired medium, which is then searched in the database. If the medium is available, the user is identified, the medium is lent, and the process ends with the medium being lent.

If the medium is not available, a message is sent to the library user. The user is then asked whether they want to reserve the medium. If the user confirms, the reservation process is started, and the process ends with the reservation process completed. If the user rejects the reservation option, the lending process is aborted, and the process ends with the lending process being aborted.

The process begins when the Warehouse Supervisor at the FMCG Company sends a request for sample products to the Supplier.

Upon receiving this request, the Supplier provides sample products, which are then sent to the Warehouse Supervisor for evaluation.

The Warehouse Supervisor evaluates the sample products and determines whether they meet the requirements. If the sample does not meet requirements, the Warehouse Supervisor adjusts the product specifications and communicates these changes back to the Supplier, who then provides new sample products. This cycle continues until the sample meets the requirements.

Once the sample meets requirements, the Warehouse Supervisor selects the product. The Supplier then sends a purchase order to their own operations, prompting them to check stock availability.

If stock is not available, the Supplier restocks their inventory and then checks stock availability again. This continues until stock becomes available.

When stock is available, the Supplier sends the product to the FMCG Company. The Warehouse Supervisor receives the product and then checks the products against the order to verify accuracy.

If the order and physical product do not match, the Warehouse Supervisor requests the missing products from the Supplier, who then checks stock availability again and repeats the fulfillment process.

If the order and physical product match, the Warehouse Supervisor sends a payment authorization to the Supplier. The Supplier processes the payment and then notifies the supplier (confirming completion), at which point the process is completed.

First, the Online Tool for Creating Characters sends a subscription form. The applicant then selects a payment method.

Based on the chosen payment method, the process takes one of two paths. If credit card is selected, the applicant enters their credit card information. Alternatively, if bank account is selected, the applicant enters their IBAN and BIC numbers.

After either payment detail entry is completed, the paths merge and the applicant submits the information.

Once the information is submitted, the Online Tool for Creating Characters activates the WoW subscription, and the process concludes with the WoW subscription ended.

The process begins within the Learning Progress Process, involving both Teachers and Students working in parallel.

At the start, two activities commence simultaneously: Teachers activate learning progress in selected objects, while Students click on Learning Progress for each object.

After clicking on Learning Learning Progress for each object, a decision is made regarding whether the learning progress should be set manually or automatically. If the manual option is chosen, Students set the learning progress manually by themselves. If the automatic option is selected, Teachers set the learning progress automatically.

Regardless of which path is taken for setting the learning progress, the process then waits for both parallel branches to complete—the learning progress activation by Teachers and the learning progress setting (whether manual or automatic).

Once both activities are finished, the status is displayed through color markings: a red cross indicates not passed, green indicates fully processed, yellow indicates in progress, and gray indicates not started.

The process concludes after the status display is complete.

The learning progress process begins in the system and immediately splits into two parallel activities that must both be completed.

In the first parallel branch, the teacher activates the learning progress in selected objects. Simultaneously, in the second parallel branch, the student clicks on Learning Progress for each object. After the student completes this action, a decision is made regarding how the learning progress will be set. If the setting is done manually by the user, the student sets the learning progress manually. Alternatively, if the setting is done automatically by the teacher, the teacher sets the learning progress automatically. Regardless of which method is chosen, both paths converge after the learning progress has been set.

Once both parallel activities are completed—the teacher's activation of learning progress and the completion of the learning progress setting method—the process continues to determine how the status should be displayed. Based on the current state of the learning progress, one of four status displays is shown by the system: if the content has not been passed, a red cross is displayed; if the content has been fully processed, a green marking is shown; if the content is currently in progress, a yellow marking appears; or if the content has not yet been started, a gray marking is displayed.

After the appropriate status is displayed, all paths merge together and the process comes to an end.

The process begins when a customer wants a loan.

The customer fills out a credit application and then sends the application to a mediation agency. The mediation agency receives the application and forwards it to two banks simultaneously: Bank A and Bank B.

At Bank B, the loan request is received and the loan amount is checked. If the customer's income is not between €2,000 and €100,000, a rejection is sent. If the income is within this range, the bank checks if the loan amount is greater than 20 times the monthly income. If it exceeds this threshold, a rejection is sent. If the loan amount is acceptable, the bank determines an interest rate and sends a credit report.

At Bank A, the loan request is also received and the loan amount is checked. If the loan amount is greater than 20 times the monthly income, a rejection is sent. Otherwise, the bank estimates a 20% interest rate per year and sends a credit report.

The mediation agency waits to receive the rejections or credit reports from both banks. Once responses from both banks have been collected, the agency forwards the results to the customer.

The customer then receives either a rejection or a credit proposal. If the customer receives a rejection, the loan process is completed with the application being declined. If the customer receives a credit proposal, the loan process is completed with the customer having received loan offers to consider.

The process begins at SoKnow when a conflict occurs involving an employee.

The employee seeks out the mediator to address the situation. The HR Department then listens to the employee to understand the nature of the conflict. After hearing the employee's concerns, the HR Department schedules an appointment for further discussion.

The employee attends the appointment and describes the conflict in detail. Following this, the HR Department seeks a solution for the conflict and then checks if the conflict has been resolved.

If the conflict is resolved, the process concludes successfully with the conflict being resolved.

If the conflict is not resolved, the HR Department schedules a new appointment, and the process returns to seeking a solution for the conflict. This cycle of seeking solutions, checking resolution, and potentially scheduling new appointments continues until the conflict is finally resolved.

The process begins when there is a need to purchase office supplies.

First, the requirement is recorded. Then, offers are obtained and reviewed.

After reviewing the offers, a decision is made based on whether the offer exceeds €2000. If the offer exceeds €2000, it must be approved before proceeding. If the offer does not exceed €2000, the process moves directly to ordering the goods.

Once the goods are ordered, the process checks whether the delivery arrives on time. If the delivery is not on time, a new delivery deadline is set, and the process loops back to check again whether the delivery has arrived on time. This continues until the delivery is received on time.

When the delivery arrives on time, a final acceptance of the goods is conducted. The goods are then sent to goods receipt, where the delivery is inspected.

After inspection, a check is made to determine whether the delivery is complete. If the delivery is complete, the delivery is confirmed, payment is initiated, and the payment is forwarded to Accounting/Controlling. The process then ends with the office supplies successfully purchased.

If the delivery is not complete, the supplier is contacted and asked for a new delivery. The process then returns to checking whether the delivery arrives on time, repeating the cycle until a complete delivery is received and processed.

The process begins when a customer wants to resolve an issue.

The customer first recognizes the problem, then contacts customer service, and describes the problem. This problem description is communicated to the Consultation Team in Customer Service.

Upon receiving the problem description, the Consultation Team identifies the problem, finds a suitable solution, and describes the solution back to the customer.

The customer then attempts to fix the problem based on the provided solution. After attempting the fix, the customer evaluates whether the solution was helpful.

If the solution is helpful, the customer implements the solution and the process concludes with the problem being resolved.

If the solution is not helpful, the customer requests a new solution. This request is communicated to the Consultation Team, who then suggests further solutions. The Consultation Team's response is sent back to the customer.

At this point, the customer evaluates whether the new solution is helpful. If the new solution is helpful, the process concludes with the problem being resolved. If the new solution is still not helpful, the Consultation Team continues to suggest further solutions until a satisfactory resolution is reached, at which point the process ends with the problem being resolved.

The Customer Service Operator then checks the data provided by the user. Based on this review, a decision is made regarding whether the data is complete.

If the data is not complete, the Taxi System sends a cancellation message to the customer, and the process ends with the cancellation being sent.

If the data is complete, the Customer Service Operator checks for available cars. The Taxi System then verifies if any cars will be available within the next 30 minutes.

If no cars are available within that timeframe, the Taxi System sends a cancellation message to the customer, and the process ends indicating that no cars are available.

If a car is available, the Taxi System displays a list of options. The Customer Service Operator then picks the nearest car to the client. Following this selection, the Taxi System calculates the time of arrival.

The Customer Service Operator then books the taxi, after which the Taxi System sends a booking confirmation to the customer. The process concludes with the booking being confirmed.

The process at ACME AG begins when parts are required in the Department.

First, the Department checks if the parts are in stock. Based on this assessment, the process takes one of two paths.

If the parts are in stock, they are retrieved from storage, and the process concludes with the parts being successfully retrieved from storage.

If the parts are not in stock, the Department specifies and quantifies the requirements, then completes a purchase order. This purchase order is then sent to Central Purchasing, where it is checked.

After checking the purchase order, Central Purchasing determines whether the vendor is known. If the vendor is known, an order template is created from the purchase order. If the vendor is not known, a new vendor is created first. Both paths then converge.

The purchase order is then forwarded to the Approver for approval. Once the purchase order is approved, it returns to Central Purchasing for the receipt of goods. Upon successful receipt, the process ends with the parts being procured.

However, if delivery problems occur during the receipt of goods, the order status is adjusted by Central Purchasing, and the process ends with the order being cancelled due to delivery issues.

The process begins when an applicant starts creating an application. Once the application is created, it is sent to the loan provider, who receives the application.

After receiving the application, the loan provider controls the document to verify its contents. A decision is then made regarding whether the document is complete.

If the document is complete, the loan provider accepts the document, and the process ends with the providing being completed.

If the document is incomplete, the loan provider returns the document to the applicant. The applicant then completes the missing information and sends the updated document back to the loan provider. The loan provider admits the document, and the process ends with the providing being completed.

Throughout this process, there are three communications between the applicant and the loan provider: first when the application is initially sent, second when the incomplete document is returned to the applicant, and third when the applicant sends the completed information back to the loan provider.

The process begins within the HR Department, where HR Staff are responsible for all activities.

The process starts with securing the personnel development needs, followed by analyzing employee data. After the analysis is complete, three activities are performed simultaneously: checking personnel capacity, determining capacity requirements, and identifying training opportunities. All three of these activities must be completed before the process can continue.

Once these parallel activities are finished, an employee interview is conducted. Following the interview, three more activities occur in parallel: considering training requests, considering improvement suggestions, and allocating training. Again, all three of these activities must be completed before proceeding.

After these parallel tasks are finished, the HR Staff discusses the findings with the department head. Subsequently, the training or continuing education is organized, and the competency profile is updated. The process concludes with securing the personnel development needs once more, after which the process ends.

Finally, HR Staff secure the personnel development needs once more, ensuring that the cycle of development planning is complete and documented. The process then concludes.

First, HR secures the personnel development needs, followed by analyzing employee data to understand the current workforce situation.

After the analysis, three activities are carried out simultaneously: checking personnel capacity, determining capacity requirements, and identifying training opportunities. All three of these activities must be completed before the process can continue.

Once these parallel activities are finished, HR conducts an employee interview to gather direct input from staff members.

Following the interview, three more activities occur in parallel: considering training requests, considering improvement suggestions, and allocating training. These three tasks are all performed concurrently and must all be completed before moving forward.

After these parallel considerations are complete, HR discusses the findings and decisions with the department head. Subsequently, the training and continuing education activities are organized based on the outcomes of these discussions.

The competency profile is then updated to reflect any changes or new skills acquired. Finally, HR secures the personnel development needs once more to ensure all requirements have been addressed and documented, bringing the process to its conclusion.

The process begins at SoKnow's Development Department when a new order is initiated.

First, the order intake is performed, followed by describing the requirements. A workshop is then conducted to gather more detailed information, after which a project sketch is created.

At this point, the Development Department waits to receive an appointment confirmation from the Customer Company. The Customer sends this appointment confirmation, which triggers the next phase.

Once the appointment confirmation is received, a customer conversation is conducted. Following this discussion, a specification sheet is written and sent to the customer. The Customer at the Customer Company receives this specification sheet and provides feedback, which is then received by the Development Department.

After receiving the customer feedback, project and capacity planning is performed. Standard open-source products are checked, use cases are defined, and costs are calculated.

A decision is then made whether to develop new products or use existing ones. If existing products are to be used, the knowledge management systems are adjusted. If new products need to be developed, product development takes place. Both paths converge afterward.

The product acceptance is then performed by the Development Department, and simultaneously the Customer participates in this product acceptance. The Customer's participation feeds back into the process, allowing the Development Department to obtain customer feedback.

Finally, follow-up projects are identified, and the process concludes with the order being completed.

The online selling process begins when the Seller starts the process by displaying items on a webpage. This information is communicated to the Buyer, who can then purchase an item. The Buyer's purchase triggers a communication to the Seller, who receives the buyer's order.

Upon receiving the order, the Seller sends an order purchase confirmation back to the Buyer. Following this, the Seller sends the order to the Shipping Company. The Shipping Company receives this order and proceeds to get the item.

After obtaining the item, a decision point is reached regarding delivery. If the Shipping Company can deliver within proper dates, they deliver the item to the customer. This delivery is communicated to the Buyer, and simultaneously, eBay tracks the order. Once tracking is complete, the Buyer closes the order, and the process ends with the order being closed.

However, if the Shipping Company does not deliver the item, the Buyer faces a decision. The Buyer can either ask for money reimbursement or request reshipment of the item.

If the Buyer chooses to ask for money reimbursement, this request is communicated to the Seller, who receives the buyer's decision. The Seller then reimburses the money, and the process ends with an escalation.

Alternatively, if the Buyer requests reshipment, this request is communicated back to the Seller, who sends the order to the Shipping Company again, restarting the delivery portion of the process.

The process at SoKnow begins in the Development Department when an order is received.

First, the order intake is performed, followed by the purchase of a knowledge management system. Once the system is purchased, adjustment requests are received from the customer company. Based on these requests, adjustments are made to the system, and then a notification is sent to the customer company informing them of the changes.

Next, a search for a test group is conducted, and once identified, tests are carried out with this group. After testing, the test results are evaluated.

If the results are negative, further adjustments are made and the tests are conducted again. This cycle continues until positive results are achieved.

Once the test results are positive, test group workshops are conducted, followed by training of employees on the system. After training is complete, the development department is informed about any adjustment requests that may have emerged.

If adjustment requests exist, the necessary adjustments are made before proceeding. If there are no adjustment requests, the process continues directly.

The customer is then informed that the product is finished, and a check is performed to determine if the adjustments are satisfactory.

If the adjustments are not satisfactory, the process loops back to making adjustments based on the customer company's requests, and the subsequent steps are repeated including notification, testing, workshops, training, and customer review.

If the adjustments are satisfactory, the knowledge management system is implemented, and the process concludes with the order being completed.
